title: Light Ring
statementMd:
There are $n$ lights in a circle, numbered from $1$ to $n$ clockwise. Light $i$ initially has state $a_i$: `0` means off and `1` means on.

In one operation, choose a starting light $i$, pay $c_i$, and toggle exactly $k$ consecutive lights clockwise starting from it. Toggling changes `0` to `1` and `1` to `0`; light $n$ is followed by light $1$. Any number of operations, including zero, is allowed.

Find the minimum total cost to turn all lights off.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $T$ ($1 \le T \le 10000$). Description of the test cases follows.

The first line contains two integers $n$ and $k$ ($1 \le k \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$).

The second line contains a binary string $a$ of length $n$. Its $i$-th character is the initial state of light $i$.

The third line contains $n$ integers $c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_n$ ($1 \le c_i \le 10^9$), giving the operation cost for each starting position.

The sum of $n$ over all test cases does not exceed $2 \cdot 10^5$.

## Output

For each test case, output one line containing the answer.

Print one integer: the minimum total cost to turn all lights off.

If there is no solution, print a single integer $-1$.

## Note

In the first test case, starting at light $3$ toggles lights $3$ and $4$ and costs $7$.

In the second test case, each operation toggles $2$ lights, so the parity of the number of lights that are on does not change. Initially, $1$ light is on, so it is impossible to turn all lights off.

In the third test case, operating once from each of lights $2,3,4,5,6$ costs $5$, whereas operating from light $1$ costs $100$.

In the fourth test case, the only light is initially off. No operations are needed, so the minimum cost is $0$.
